83401.e: Many smoke alarms give a short beep when the battery gets weak. Then it needs changing soon.
83401.m: A short beep often means a weak battery.

83402.q: How often should you check a smoke alarm?
a: Only when there is a fire
83402.e: Only a working smoke alarm can warn you. That is why you check it regularly with the test button.

83403.q: What shape are the hazard symbols on chemicals?
83403.e: The hazard symbols are diamonds, that is squares standing on one corner. Inside is a black picture.

83404.q: What colour is the border of a hazard symbol?
83404.e: Hazard symbols have a red border and a white background. The black picture shows the danger.
83404.m: Hazard symbols have a red border.

83405.q: What does the hazard symbol with a flame mean?
83405.e: The flame shows that this substance can catch fire easily. Keep it away from heat and flames.
83405.m: The flame symbol warns of highly flammable substances.

83406.q: What does the hazard symbol with a skull and crossbones mean?
83406.e: The skull and crossbones warns of very poisonous substances. Even small amounts can be deadly.
83406.m: The skull and crossbones warns of poison.

83407.q: What does the hazard symbol with a dead tree and a fish mean?
83407.e: This substance harms animals and plants, especially in water. It must not go down the drain.
83407.m: The tree and fish warn of danger to the environment.

83408.q: What does the hazard symbol with an exploding bomb mean?
83408.e: The exploding bomb warns of substances that can explode. You have to be very careful with them.
83408.m: The bomb warns of explosive substances.

83409.q: What does the hazard symbol with a flame over a circle mean?
83409.e: Such substances give off oxygen. They make a fire stronger, even if they do not burn themselves.
83409.m: The flame over a circle warns of oxidising substances.

83410.q: On which things at home do you often find hazard symbols?
83410.e: Many cleaning products contain dangerous substances. That is why they carry hazard symbols.
83410.m: Many cleaning products carry hazard symbols.

83411.q: What does the hazard symbol with drops attacking a hand mean?
83411.e: Corrosive substances can injure skin and eyes. That is why the symbol shows a hand being attacked.
83411.m: The symbol with the hand warns of corrosive substances.

83412.q: What is the first thing you do in a fire?
83412.e: The rule is: raise the alarm, rescue, put out. First you call for help, then you get people to safety.
83412.m: In a fire, first raise the alarm, then rescue, then put it out.

83413.q: What should you do if your own clothes are on fire?
83413.e: Running gives the fire more air. If you lie down and roll, you smother the flames.
83413.m: If your clothes are on fire, lie down and roll.

83414.q: What do you use to get out of a building on fire?
83414.e: The lift can get stuck in a fire. That is why you always take the stairs.
83414.m: In a fire, take the stairs, never the lift.

83415.q: Why do you close the door when leaving a room on fire?
a: It holds back smoke and fire
83415.e: A closed door slows down smoke and flames. That way the escape route stays clear for longer.
83415.m: A closed door slows down smoke and fire.

83416.q: What colour are emergency exit signs?
83416.e: Emergency exits and escape routes are marked with green signs. They show a white figure running to a door.

83417.q: What should you not do when escaping from a fire?
83417.e: Looking for things wastes precious time. People are more important than things.
83417.m: In a fire, save yourself, not your toys.

83418.q: Where does everyone meet during a fire drill at school?
83418.e: After leaving the school building, everyone goes to the assembly point. There the teacher can see whether everyone is there.
83418.m: After a fire alarm, everyone meets at the assembly point.

83419.q: Who comes in red vehicles to put out fires?
83419.e: The fire brigade drives red vehicles with blue lights. It puts out fires and rescues people.
83419.m: The fire brigade puts out fires and rescues people.

83420.q: What is barbecue charcoal made from?
83420.e: Barbecue charcoal is charcoal made from wood. Wood is heated with little air until it turns into charcoal.
83420.m: Barbecue charcoal is made from wood.

83421.q: What is the job of people who make charcoal called?
83421.e: Charcoal burners turn wood into charcoal in a big pile. In the Entlebuch in the canton of Lucerne there are still charcoal burners today.

83422.q: What is the big pile of wood in which charcoal burners make charcoal called?
83422.e: In a charcoal kiln, wood is covered with earth. It smoulders there for days with little air and turns into charcoal.
83422.m: In a charcoal kiln, wood turns into charcoal.

83423.q: What must you never pour onto glowing barbecue charcoal?
83423.e: Methylated spirits and petrol evaporate and catch fire explosively. A dangerous jet of flame shoots up.
83423.m: Never pour methylated spirits or petrol onto glowing charcoal.

83424.q: How can you tell that the barbecue charcoal is ready for grilling?
a: It is covered in grey ash
83424.e: When the charcoal is glowing right through, a grey layer lies on it. Then it gives off even heat.
83424.m: Grey charcoal is ready for grilling.

83425.q: Why must you never use a charcoal barbecue in a closed room?
a: The charcoal goes out at once
83425.e: Glowing charcoal produces carbon monoxide. This gas is poisonous and you cannot smell it.
83425.m: A charcoal barbecue belongs outdoors only.

83426.q: What do you use to light barbecue charcoal safely?
83426.e: Firelighters burn slowly and evenly. That way the charcoal lights without a jet of flame.

83427.q: What do you use to turn sausages on a hot barbecue?
83427.e: Barbecue tongs are long and made of metal. That way your fingers stay well away from the embers.

83626.q: You count how many bikes are in front of the school. What are you doing?
83626.e: When you count, measure or ask and write down the result, you are collecting data.
83626.m: Counting and writing it down means collecting data.

83627.q: What is the easiest way to count how many red cars drive past?
83627.e: For each red car you draw a line. At the end you count the lines.
83627.m: With a tally chart you can count quickly and easily.

83628.q: How do you write the number 5 on a tally chart?
a: Four lines and one line across
83628.e: You draw four lines and cross them through with the fifth line. That makes bundles of five.
83628.m: On a tally chart you always bundle five lines.

83629.q: A tally chart shows two bundles of five and three lines. How many is that?
83629.e: Two bundles of five are 10, plus 3 lines. 10 + 3 makes 13.
83629.m: Bundles of five help you add up quickly.

83630.q: What is best for measuring how tall a plant is?
83630.e: You measure lengths with a ruler or tape measure. Then you write down the number.
83630.m: To collect data you need the right measuring tool.

83631.q: What do you use to collect data about the weather, for example the temperature?
83631.e: A thermometer shows how warm or cold it is. You can write down the reading every day.

83632.q: Why do you write down data you have collected?
a: So you do not forget it
83632.e: What you write down you can read again later, compare and analyse.
83632.m: Data that is written down can be looked at again later.

83633.q: Every day you check whether the sun is shining. How long should you do this to get a good overview?
83633.e: The longer you observe, the more data you have. Then you see whether it is often or rarely sunny.

83634.q: Where do you enter numbers you have collected so they are clear?
83634.e: A table has rows and columns. That way you can find each number again quickly.
83634.m: In a table, data stands neatly in rows and columns.

83635.q: What do you write down before you go shopping?
83635.e: On a shopping list you write one below the other what you want to buy. That way you do not forget anything.
83635.m: A shopping list helps you not to forget anything.

83636.q: How are things usually written on a list?
a: Drawn on top of each other
83636.e: On a list you write each item on its own line, one below the other.
83636.m: On a list each item has its own line.

83637.q: What do you call a single thing on a list?
83637.e: Each thing written on the list is an item.
83637.m: A list is made up of single items.

83638.q: Your shopping list has bread, milk, cheese and apples. How many items are there?
83638.e: Bread, milk, cheese and apples are four things, so four items.
83638.m: You can count the items on a list.

83639.q: What do you do with an item on your to-do list when the task is done?
83639.e: With a tick you see straight away what is already done and what is still missing.
83639.m: You tick off finished tasks on the list.

83640.q: Which list shows which children are in the class?
83640.e: The class list has the names of all the children in a class.
83640.m: The class list names all the children in a class.

83641.q: You have a list with 6 names and cross out 2. How many names are left?
83641.e: 6 minus 2 makes 4. Four names are not crossed out yet.

83642.q: What is on a guest list for a party?
83642.e: A guest list shows who is invited to the party.
83642.m: The guest list has all the invited guests.

83643.q: Why do you number the items on a list 1, 2, 3 and so on?
83643.e: With numbers you see straight away how many items there are, and you can name each one exactly.

83644.q: Which name comes first in alphabetical order: Lea, Ben or Mia?
83644.e: You look at the first letter. B comes before L and M.
83644.m: When sorting alphabetically, the first letter counts first.

83646.q: Which letter comes directly before F in the alphabet?
83646.e: The order is C, D, E, F, G. So E comes before F.
83646.m: If you know the alphabet well, you find neighbouring letters quickly.

83647.q: How many letters does the alphabet have?
83647.e: The alphabet goes from A to Z and has 26 letters.

83648.q: Which letter comes directly after M in the alphabet?
83648.e: The order is K, L, M, N, O. So N comes after M.
83648.m: You need to know the alphabet by heart to sort well.

83649.q: Which city comes last in alphabetical order: Bern, Zurich or Lucerne?
83649.e: Z is the last letter of the alphabet. That is why Zurich comes after Bern and Lucerne.
83649.m: Words with Z come right at the end.

83652.q: You have buttons in red, blue and yellow. How can you group them?
83652.e: All the red buttons go together, and so do all the blue and all the yellow ones.
83652.m: When grouping, things that have something in common go together.

83653.q: Which thing does not fit in the group: apple, pear, banana, hammer?
83653.e: Apple, pear and banana are fruit. A hammer is a tool.
83653.m: When you group things, you also see what does not belong.

83654.q: What do a dog, a cat and a rabbit have in common?
83654.e: Dog, cat and rabbit all belong to the group of animals.
83654.m: Things in a group share a feature.

83655.q: You have 12 children and make groups of 3. How many groups are there?
83655.e: 12 divided into groups of 3 makes 4 groups, because 4 · 3 makes 12.
83655.m: To share into equal groups you divide.

83656.q: How can you group building blocks?
83656.e: You can sort building blocks into cubes, cuboids and cylinders, for example.
83656.m: Shapes, colours and sizes are good for grouping.

83657.e: Bike, bus and train are all vehicles. Each of the other groups has something else in it.
83657.m: In a group, all the things go together.

83658.q: When you sort things into groups, what becomes easier?
83658.e: If you know which group something is in, you find it more quickly.

83659.q: Which animal does not fit with the others: eagle, sparrow, blackbird, trout?
83659.e: Eagle, sparrow and blackbird are birds. The trout is a fish.

83660.q: What does a Venn diagram show?
83660.e: In a Venn diagram you draw circles. Into each circle go the things that belong to the same set.
83660.m: A Venn diagram shows groups as circles.

83661.q: How do you usually draw a set in a Venn diagram?
83661.e: A closed line like a circle surrounds all the things that belong to the set.
83661.m: You draw a set with a closed line.

83662.q: One circle is called “red”, another “round”. Where does a red ball go?
83662.e: A red ball is red and round. That is why it belongs in both circles, so in the shared part.
83662.m: Something that belongs to two sets goes in the overlap.

83663.q: A circle is called “animals”. Where does a stone go?
83663.e: A stone is not an animal. That is why it does not belong in the circle “animals”.
83663.m: Something that does not belong to the set goes outside.

83664.q: Circles “can fly” and “has feathers”: where does a duck go?
83664.e: A duck can fly and has feathers. So it goes in the shared part of the two circles.
83664.m: One thing can be in several sets at the same time.

83665.q: Circles “can fly” and “has feathers”: where does a penguin go?
83665.e: A penguin has feathers but cannot fly. That is why it goes only in the circle “has feathers”.

83666.q: The circle “even numbers” contains 2, 4 and 6. Where does 8 go?
83666.e: 8 is an even number, just like 2, 4 and 6. So it goes in the circle.
83666.m: Numbers can also be sorted into sets.

83667.q: The circle “children with a bike” has 5 children, the circle “children with a scooter” has 4. Two children are in both circles. How many children have a bike but no scooter?
83667.e: Of the 5 children with a bike, 2 also have a scooter. 5 minus 2 makes 3.
83667.m: You have to pay attention to the overlap when counting.

83668.q: What does a family tree show?
83668.e: A family tree shows the family: parents, children, grandparents and so on.
83668.m: A family tree shows how a family is related.

83669.q: What do you call your parents' parents?
83669.e: The mother and father of your mother or father are your grandparents.
83669.m: Your parents' parents are your grandparents.

83670.q: What do you call children with the same parents?
83670.m: Brothers and sisters are called siblings.

83671.e: The children of your aunt and uncle are your cousins.
83671.m: The children of your uncle and aunt are your cousins.

83672.q: How many grandparents does a person have?
83672.e: Every person has two parents, and each parent has two parents too. 2 + 2 makes 4.

83673.e: Your parents' sisters are your aunts.
83673.m: Your mother's or father's sister is an aunt.

83674.q: Where in a family tree are the oldest relatives often shown?
83674.e: Often the oldest are at the top and the younger family members below. But some family trees are drawn the other way round.
83674.m: A family tree arranges the family by generations.

83675.q: What do you call the children of your children?
83675.e: For grandparents, the children of their children are their grandchildren.
83675.m: The children of your own children are your grandchildren.

83676.q: What do you need a dictionary for?
a: To look up how to spell a word
83676.e: In a dictionary you find the correct spelling and often the meaning of words too.
83676.m: You look up words in a dictionary.

83677.q: You are looking up “zebra” in a dictionary. Where do you look?
83677.e: Z is the last letter of the alphabet. That is why words with Z are right at the back.
83677.m: You find words with Z at the back of the dictionary.

83678.q: You are looking up “ant” in a dictionary. Where do you look?
83678.e: A is the first letter of the alphabet. Words with A are at the beginning.
83678.m: You find words with A at the front of the dictionary.

83679.q: What are the words at the top of a dictionary page for?
a: They show which words are on the page
They show the colour of the page
83679.e: At the top there is often the first or last word on the page. That way you quickly see whether the word you want is on this page.
83679.m: The guide words at the top show which words are on a page.

83680.q: You are looking for “cat”. The page starts with “camel” and ends with “canoe”. What do you do?
83680.e: In “cat”, t comes after n. So “cat” comes after “canoe”, further back in the dictionary.
83680.m: When looking things up, you compare letter by letter.

83681.q: In which form do you usually find “went” in the dictionary?
83681.e: Verbs are usually listed in their basic form in the dictionary. So for “went” you look up “go”.
83681.m: You look up verbs in the dictionary in their basic form.

83682.q: In which form do you usually find “mice” in the dictionary?
83682.e: Nouns are listed in the singular in the dictionary. For “mice” you look up “mouse”.
83682.m: You look up nouns in the dictionary in the singular.

83683.q: What is the name of a well-known German dictionary that is also used in Swiss schools?
83683.e: The Duden is a well-known dictionary for German spelling.
83683.m: The Duden shows the correct spelling of German words.

a: A list of all the books in the library
83684.e: The catalogue shows which books the library has and where they are.
83684.m: In the library catalogue you find all the books in a library.

83685.q: What can you search for in the library catalogue?
83685.e: You can search by the title of the book, the name of the author or a topic.
83685.m: In the catalogue you search by title, author or topic.

83686.q: What do you usually need to borrow a book from the library?
83686.e: With the card, the library knows who has borrowed the book.
83686.m: You borrow books with a library card.

83687.q: What is the small sticker with letters and numbers on the spine of a book, which shows where the book belongs, called?
83687.e: The shelf mark is like an address. It shows which shelf the book belongs on.
83687.m: The shelf mark shows a book's place on the shelf.

83688.q: How do many libraries search their catalogue today?
83688.e: In the past there were index cards in drawers. Today the catalogue is usually stored on a computer.
83688.m: Today the library catalogue is usually on the computer.

83689.q: What must you do when the loan period of a book is over?
83689.e: Borrowed books belong to the library. After the loan period you take them back so that others can read them too.
83689.m: You return borrowed books on time.

83690.q: What does the catalogue show when a book is currently on loan?
a: That it is not on the shelf
83690.e: The catalogue shows whether a book is available or currently on loan.
83690.m: The catalogue tells you whether a book is there right now.

83691.q: Before there were computers, where was the information about the books written?
83691.e: There was an index card for each book. The cards were kept in order in drawers.
83691.m: In the past a library catalogue was made of lots of index cards.

83692.q: Why do you stick a label on a box?
a: So you know what is inside
83692.e: The label says what is in the box. That way you do not have to open it.
83692.m: A label shows what is in a box.

83693.q: What is often written on the label on your exercise book?
83693.e: With your name and the subject, everyone knows straight away whose book it is and what it is for.
83693.m: The label on an exercise book shows name and subject.

83694.q: What is on the label of a yoghurt in the shop?
a: The use-by date and the ingredients
83694.e: Food packaging shows, for example, the ingredients and when you should eat it by.
83694.m: Labels in the shop show important information about the goods.

83695.q: A jar says “Sugar”, but there is salt inside. What is wrong?
83695.e: A label must match what is inside. Otherwise it is misleading.
83695.m: A label must always match what is inside.

83696.q: What does the label in your T-shirt often show?
83696.e: The label in clothes shows, for example, the size and how to wash them.
83696.m: Clothes labels show size and care.

83697.q: The boxes in the classroom have labels: “Pens”, “Scissors”, “Glue”. Where do you put a pair of scissors?
83697.e: The label shows what belongs in the box. Scissors belong in the box “Scissors”.
83697.m: Labels help you put things away in the right place.

83698.q: What on a label helps children who cannot read yet?
83698.e: A picture, for example of a pen, shows what is in the box even without reading.
83698.m: You can understand pictures on labels without reading.

83699.q: What is on a label on a suitcase at the airport?
a: Where the suitcase is travelling to
83699.e: The luggage label shows the destination. That way the suitcase is loaded onto the right plane.
83699.m: A luggage label gets the suitcase to the right destination.

83700.q: Which category does the tulip belong to?
83700.e: The tulip is a flower. That is why it belongs to the category flowers.
83700.m: A category groups similar things under one name.

83701.q: Which category does the guitar belong to?
83701.e: You make music with a guitar. It belongs to the musical instruments.
83701.m: Musical instruments form their own category.

83702.q: Which word is the name of a category?
83702.e: Carrot, leek and pea are single things. Vegetables is the general term, so the category.
83702.m: The name of a category is a general term.

83703.e: You put on a jumper. Plate, scissors and spoon are not clothes.
83703.m: Clothes are everything you put on.

83704.q: What does NOT belong in the category “furniture”?
83704.e: Table, chair and wardrobe are furniture. A banana is a fruit.
83704.m: Not everything fits into every category.

83705.q: In which category do you find a book about dinosaurs in the library?
83705.e: A book that explains real facts about dinosaurs is a non-fiction book.
83705.m: Books with real facts belong to non-fiction.

83706.q: Which category does orange juice belong to?
83706.e: You drink orange juice. That is why it belongs to drinks.
83706.m: Everything you drink belongs to the category drinks.

83707.q: Why are there categories in the shop like “bread”, “dairy” or “vegetables”?
83707.e: When similar goods are together, you know where to look.
83707.m: Categories help you find things quickly.

83708.q: What is in a fact file about an animal?
a: Important facts like size and food
83708.e: A fact file contains short, important facts, for example name, size, habitat and food.
83708.m: A fact file sums up important facts briefly.

83709.q: What belongs in a fact file about you?
83709.e: A personal fact file has details like name, age, hobbies and favourite food.
83709.m: A fact file about you has your name and age.

83710.q: How are the facts in a fact file usually written?
83710.e: You should be able to read a fact file quickly. That is why you write short key words one below the other.
83710.m: A fact file is short and clear.

83711.q: Which fact fits under “Food” in a squirrel's fact file?
83711.e: Squirrels like to eat nuts, seeds and buds. The other words describe something else, for example the colour or the size.
83711.m: Each fact belongs under the right heading.

83712.q: What is often shown on a fact file as well?
83712.e: A photo or drawing shows straight away what the animal or person looks like.
83712.m: A picture makes a fact file clearer.

83713.q: Which detail should you NOT write in a fact file that is on the internet?
83713.e: Your address is private. Strangers should not know where you live.
83713.m: Private details like my address do not belong on the internet.

83714.q: A fact file says: “lives in water, has fins, breathes with gills”. Which animal is it?
83714.e: Fish have fins and gills. With them they can swim and breathe in water.
83714.m: With a good fact file you can recognise an animal.

83715.q: Under which heading in an animal fact file does “forest” go?
83715.e: The habitat says where an animal lives, for example in the forest, in water or in a meadow.
83715.m: The habitat shows where an animal is at home.

83716.q: In the past, what did the police use wanted posters describing a person for?
a: To find people they were looking for
83716.e: In the past the police searched for people with wanted posters. They showed what the person looked like and their features.
83716.m: A description like this lets people recognise someone.

83717.q: What do you do in a survey?
a: Ask lots of people the same thing
Read a book on your own
83717.e: In a survey you ask several people the same question and collect the answers.
83717.m: In a survey you ask lots of people the same thing.

83718.q: Which question is good for a survey in the class?
a: How many legs does a dog have?
83718.e: With this question, each child gives a different answer. The other questions have only one correct answer.
83718.m: A good survey question can be answered in different ways.

83719.q: In a survey, 8 children say “pizza”, 5 “spaghetti” and 3 “soup”. What is the most popular?
83719.e: Pizza has the most answers, with 8 votes.
83719.m: The answer with the most votes is the most popular.

83720.q: In a survey, 8 children say “pizza”, 5 “spaghetti” and 3 “soup”. How many children were asked?
83720.e: 8 + 5 + 3 makes 16. That is how many children answered.
83720.m: If you add up all the answers, you know how many took part.

83721.q: What is a good way to show the results of a survey?
83721.e: In a bar chart each bar is as tall as the number of votes. That way you see straight away what is most common.
83721.m: A bar chart shows survey results at a glance.

83722.q: What is important in a survey?
a: You only ask your best friends
Whoever answers first gets two votes
83722.e: If someone counts more than once or only friends are asked, the result is no longer right.
83722.m: In a fair survey each vote counts only once.

83723.q: In a survey, the bars are 6 for “cat” and 9 for “dog”. How many more votes does “dog” have?
83723.e: 9 minus 6 makes 3. So the dog has 3 more votes.
83723.m: You find differences in a chart by subtracting.

83724.q: What must you NOT do in a survey?
83724.e: The answers must stay exactly as people gave them. Otherwise the survey is wrong.
83724.m: You always report survey answers honestly.

83725.q: How can you vote quickly in a class survey?
a: You send each child a letter
83725.e: Everyone who chooses an answer raises their hand. Then you count the hands.
83725.m: You can vote quickly by raising your hand.

84222.q: What does the term climate change mean?
a: The Earth's climate changes over a long time
The weather changes from one day to the next
84222.e: In climate change, the typical weather changes over many decades. Today the Earth is mainly getting warmer.
84222.m: Climate change means that the climate changes over a long time.

84223.q: Because of today's climate change, is the Earth getting warmer or colder on average?
84223.e: The Earth's average temperature has risen clearly over the last 150 years. That is why people also speak of global warming.
84223.m: Climate change is making the Earth warmer.

84224.q: Which human activity contributes especially strongly to climate change?
84224.e: Burning coal, oil and gas produces exhaust gases that hold heat in the air. This makes it warmer.
84224.m: Burning coal, oil and gas heats up the climate.

84226.q: What is an especially climate-friendly way to get to school?
84226.e: Walking or cycling produces no exhaust gases. It also keeps you fit.
84226.m: Walking or cycling is good for the climate.

84227.q: Because of climate change, what is happening to snow at low altitudes in Switzerland?
a: There is the same amount of snow
84227.e: Because it is warmer, rain falls more often instead of snow on the Central Plateau. Many low-lying ski areas are also short of snow.
84227.m: There is less snow in the lowlands today than in the past.

84228.q: Why do trees help against climate change?
a: They take carbon dioxide out of the air
84228.e: Trees need carbon dioxide to grow and store it in their wood. That way less of it stays in the air.
84228.m: Trees take carbon dioxide out of the air.

84229.q: How are heatwaves in Switzerland changing because of climate change?
a: They only come in winter now
84229.e: Because it is getting warmer overall, there are more very hot days. Heatwaves therefore happen more often and get stronger.
84229.m: With climate change there are more heatwaves.

84230.q: How can you save energy at home and so help the climate?
a: Switch off the light when you leave the room
Leave the windows open in winter
Leave the TV on all the time
84230.e: Electricity and heating use energy. If you switch off lights you do not need, you save energy.

84231.q: What are parts of the Rhône Glacier covered with in summer so that it melts more slowly?
84231.e: The white sheets reflect the sunlight. Underneath them the ice melts more slowly.
84231.m: White sheets protect the ice from the sun.

84232.q: Why are the glaciers in the Alps melting?
a: Because the wind is getting stronger
84232.e: In a warmer climate, more ice melts in summer than is added by snow in winter. That is why the glaciers are getting smaller.

84233.q: Where does the meltwater of a glacier flow?
84233.e: The meltwater gathers into streams. These flow into rivers such as the Rhône or the Rhine.
84233.m: Meltwater from glaciers flows into streams and rivers.

84234.q: What often forms where a glacier has melted away?
84234.e: Meltwater collects in the hollow that the ice leaves behind. This is how new glacier lakes form.
84234.m: Where a glacier disappears, a lake often forms.

84235.q: Why does ice covered in dark dust melt faster?
a: Dark surfaces absorb more heat from the sun
84235.e: Dark surfaces absorb more sunlight and so get warmer. That is why dirty ice melts faster.
84235.m: Dark surfaces get warmer in the sun than light ones.

84236.q: Which canton is the Great Aletsch Glacier in?
84236.e: The Great Aletsch Glacier is in Upper Valais. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
84236.m: The Aletsch Glacier is in Valais.

84237.q: In which season does the most glacier ice melt?
84237.e: In summer it is warm even in the mountains. That is when the most meltwater flows out of the glacier.

84238.q: What will be missing in high summer later on, once the glaciers have disappeared?
84238.e: Glaciers release a lot of water, especially in hot, dry summers. Without them, some rivers will then carry less water.
84238.m: Glaciers are important stores of water for the summer.

a: Several very hot days in a row
A high wave in the sea
A warm wind in the evening
84239.e: In a heatwave it stays very hot for several days. Often the nights hardly cool down either.
84239.m: A heatwave is lots of hot days in a row.

84240.q: What should you definitely do in great heat?
a: Run about in the sun at midday
84240.e: In heat, your body sweats out a lot of water. That is why you need to drink regularly, even if you are not thirsty.
84240.m: In hot weather, drink lots of water.

84241.q: Where was Switzerland's highest temperature, 41.5 °C in 2003, measured?
84241.e: On 11 August 2003, 41.5 °C was measured in Grono in the Misox valley. That is still the Swiss record today (as of 2026).
84241.m: The Swiss heat record comes from Grono.

84242.q: What is a day called when the temperature reaches at least 30 °C?
84242.e: From 30 °C, it is called a hot day. A summer day, on the other hand, only needs 25 °C.
84242.m: On a hot day it reaches at least 30 degrees.

84243.q: What is a night called when it does not cool down below 20 °C?
84243.e: On a tropical night it stays as warm as in the tropics. Many people sleep badly then.
84243.m: On a tropical night it stays above 20 degrees.

84244.q: Who is especially at risk during a heatwave?
84244.e: The bodies of babies and older people are less able to cool down. They need special attention in hot weather.
84244.m: Babies and older people need special protection in hot weather.

84245.q: On a hot summer's day, when is it usually hottest outside?
84245.e: The sun heats the ground and the air all day long. That is why it usually gets warmest in the afternoon.
84245.m: It is usually hottest outside in the afternoon.

84246.q: How do you keep a flat cool during the day in hot weather?
a: Open all the windows in the midday sun
84246.e: Closed shutters keep the sun out. It is best to air the rooms in the cool night or early morning.
84246.m: In hot weather, keep the shutters closed during the day.

84247.q: Which clothes are best in great heat?
84247.e: Light fabrics let air reach your skin, and pale colours heat up less. A hat also protects your head.
84247.m: In hot weather, wear light, pale clothes.

a: A long time with too little rain
84248.e: In a drought it rains too little for weeks or months. The soil, plants and rivers and lakes dry out.
84248.m: In a drought there is no rain for a long time.

84249.q: What do you often see in the ground during a drought?
84249.e: When the soil dries out, it shrinks. This makes cracks.
84249.m: In dry weather, the ground cracks.

84250.q: Why are fires in the forest often banned in very dry weather?
a: Because a forest fire can start quickly
Because the trees are asleep then
Because otherwise it starts to rain
Because the foresters are on holiday
84250.e: Dry leaves and grass burn very easily. One spark can start a big forest fire.
84250.m: In dry weather, do not light fires in the forest.

84251.q: In the drought summer of 2018, how did some cows on Swiss alpine pastures get water?
a: The army flew it in by helicopter
They licked ice from the glaciers
They drank milk instead of water
84251.e: Because springs dried up, the Swiss Army flew water up to alpine pastures by helicopter. That way the animals had enough to drink.
84251.m: In summer 2018 the army flew water to the cows.

84252.q: What happens to the plants in the fields during a drought?
84252.e: Plants need water to live. Without rain they wilt and the harvest is small.

84253.q: What happens to the water in rivers and lakes during a long dry spell?
84253.e: Without rain, less water flows in. That is why rivers and lakes get lower.
84253.m: In dry weather the water level drops.

84254.q: Why do fish in streams suffer during a drought?
a: The water gets scarce and too warm
84254.e: Shallow, warm water has less oxygen. But many fish, such as trout, need cool water.

84255.q: How can you save water in the garden in dry weather?
a: Collect rainwater and use it for watering
Leave the sprinkler on all day
Water at midday in the blazing sun
Refill the paddling pool every day
84255.e: With collected rainwater you do not need to use tap water. Watering in the evening also saves water.
84255.m: Collected rainwater helps to save water.

84256.q: What is the largest hot desert in the world?
84256.e: The Sahara is roughly as big as the USA. It is the largest hot desert on Earth.
84256.m: The Sahara is the largest hot desert in the world.

84257.q: Which animal can go a long time without water in the desert?
84257.e: Camels can go many days without drinking. They store fat in their hump.
84257.m: The camel can manage a long time without water.

84258.q: What is a place with water and palm trees in the middle of the desert called?
84258.e: In an oasis, groundwater comes to the surface. Date palms grow there and people can live there.
84258.m: An oasis is a green place with water in the desert.

84259.q: What is it often like at night in a sandy desert?
a: Just as hot as at midday
84259.e: Because there are hardly any clouds, the heat escapes quickly at night. That is why it often gets cold in the desert at night.
84259.m: It can get cold in the desert at night.

84260.q: What is the illusion called when you seem to see water in the distance in the hot desert?
84260.e: Hot air above the ground bends the light. You then see the sky reflected, and it looks like a lake.
84260.m: A mirage tricks you into seeing water in the desert.

84261.q: Which desert in Chile is one of the driest in the world?
84261.e: In parts of the Atacama no rain falls for years. It lies in South America on the Pacific coast.
84261.m: The Atacama in Chile is extremely dry.

84262.q: Which plant in American deserts stores water in its thick stem?
84262.e: Cacti store water in their fleshy stem. Their spines protect them from animals.
84262.m: A cactus stores water in its stem.

84263.q: Why is Antarctica also considered a desert?
a: Because very little precipitation falls there
Because it is made of sand
Because it is very hot there
84263.e: A desert is an area with very little precipitation. Only a little snow falls in Antarctica, so it is a cold desert.
84263.m: An icy region can be a desert too.

84264.q: On which continent is most of the Amazon rainforest?
84264.e: Most of it is in Brazil. Peru, Colombia and other countries also have a share of it.
84264.m: The Amazon rainforest is in South America.

84265.q: Which slow animal hangs upside down from branches in the rainforest?
84265.e: Sloths move very slowly and hang from branches by their long claws. They sleep many hours a day.
84265.m: The sloth hangs comfortably upside down in the tree.

84266.q: Why are many rainforests cut down?
a: To make room for fields and pastures
To make room for ski slopes
So that the animals have more light
84266.e: Rainforest is cleared to sell the timber and to create fields or cattle pastures. Many animals lose their habitat as a result.
84266.m: When rainforest is cut down, animals lose their home.

84267.q: What is the weather like in the tropical rainforest all year round?
84267.e: The tropical rainforest lies close to the equator. There it is warm all year and the air is humid.
84267.m: In the tropical rainforest it is always warm and humid.

84268.q: Which plants climb up trees in the rainforest?
84268.e: Lianas climb up tree trunks towards the light. Some animals use them like ropes.
84268.m: Lianas climb up trees in the rainforest.

84269.q: Where in the rainforest do most kinds of animals live?
84269.e: In the treetops there is lots of light, flowers and fruit. That is why especially many kinds of animals live there.
84269.m: The treetops of the rainforest are teeming with animals.

84270.q: Is there solid land under the North Pole?
a: No, there is sea with ice on top
84270.e: The North Pole lies in the middle of the Arctic Ocean. The ice on it floats on the water.
84270.m: Under the North Pole there is sea, not land.

84271.q: Which big white predator lives in the Arctic?
84271.e: The polar bear is one of the largest predators on land. Its thick fur keeps it warm.
84271.m: The polar bear lives in the Arctic.

84272.q: Roughly which direction does the needle of a compass point?
84272.e: The compass needle is a small magnet. It lines up with the Earth's magnetic field and points roughly north.

84273.q: What is it called when the sun shines even at midnight in the Arctic summer?
84273.e: In summer, close to the pole, the sun does not set for days. You can even see it at midnight.
84273.m: In the Arctic summer there is the midnight sun.

84274.q: Roughly how long does it stay dark exactly at the North Pole in winter?
84274.e: At the North Pole the sun rises only once a year and sets once. That is why day and night there each last about half a year.
84274.m: At the North Pole the night lasts half a year.

84275.q: Which people have lived in the Arctic for a long time, for example in Greenland?
84275.e: The Inuit have lived in the far north for centuries. In the past they hunted mainly seals and whales.
84275.m: The Inuit live in the Arctic.

84276.q: Which animals with antlers roam the Arctic in big herds?
84276.e: Reindeer travel in big herds across the tundra. In North America they are called caribou.
84276.m: Reindeer roam the far north in herds.

84277.q: Who was the first to reach the South Pole, in 1911?
84277.e: The Norwegian Roald Amundsen reached the South Pole with dog sleds on 14 December 1911. The Briton Robert Scott arrived about a month later.
84277.m: Roald Amundsen was the first at the South Pole.

84278.q: Which birds live in Antarctica but cannot fly?
84278.e: Penguins are excellent swimmers. Their wings have become flippers.
84278.m: Penguins cannot fly, but they are great swimmers.

84279.q: Are there polar bears in Antarctica?
a: Yes, but only on the coast
84279.e: Polar bears only live in the far north. There are none in Antarctica.
84279.m: There are no polar bears in Antarctica.

84280.q: How thick is the ice on Antarctica at its thickest points?
84280.e: At its thickest points, the ice sheet is over 4000 metres thick. That is higher than most Alpine summits.
84280.m: The ice on Antarctica is kilometres thick.

a: Only scientists in research stations, for a while
Nobody, no one may ever set foot there
84281.e: Antarctica has no permanent residents. Scientists live there in research stations for a few months.
84281.m: Only scientists live in Antarctica, for a while.

84282.q: Where was the lowest air temperature on Earth measured?
84282.e: In 1983, -89.2 °C was measured at Vostok Station in Antarctica. That is a world record.
84282.m: Antarctica is the coldest place on Earth.

84283.q: How much of an iceberg can you see above the water?
84283.e: Most of an iceberg lies under water. You only see the tip.
84283.m: You only see the tip of an iceberg.

84284.q: Is an iceberg made of salt water or fresh water?
84284.e: The ice of an iceberg formed from snow, not from frozen seawater. That is why it is not salty.
84284.m: Icebergs are made of fresh water.

84285.q: What is it called when a big piece of ice breaks off a glacier into the sea?
84285.e: In calving, a block of ice breaks off the glacier and crashes into the sea. This is how a new iceberg forms.
84285.m: When a glacier calves, an iceberg forms.

84286.q: Where do most big icebergs come from?
a: From glaciers in Greenland and Antarctica
84286.e: Big glaciers in Greenland and Antarctica flow all the way to the sea. Icebergs break off there.
84286.m: Most icebergs come from Greenland and Antarctica.

84287.q: What happens to an iceberg that drifts into warmer water?
84287.e: In warmer water the ice melts bit by bit. In the end nothing is left.
84287.m: An iceberg melts in warm water.

84288.q: What colour can very old, dense ice in an iceberg be?
84288.e: Very dense ice contains hardly any air bubbles. It absorbs red light and therefore looks blue.

a: Ice pushed together on the sea
84289.e: When wind and currents push sheets of ice together on the sea, pack ice forms. It can pile up high.
84289.m: Pack ice is sea ice pushed together.

84290.q: What are ships called that can force their way through thick ice?
84290.e: Icebreakers have a very strong hull. They drive up onto the ice and break it with their weight.
84290.m: An icebreaker breaks a path through the ice.

84291.q: What does the polar bear mainly hunt on the pack ice?
84291.e: Polar bears lie in wait for seals at breathing holes in the ice. Without sea ice they find much less food.
84291.m: Polar bears hunt seals on the ice.

84292.q: What happens to the sea ice in the Arctic every summer?
84292.e: It is warmer in summer, so part of the sea ice melts. In winter it freezes over again.
84292.m: In summer, part of the sea ice melts.

84293.q: What is a single flat sheet of ice drifting on the water called?
84293.e: Ice floes are flat pieces of sea ice. Seals like to rest on them.
84293.m: An ice floe is a flat sheet of ice on the water.

84294.q: Why did the explorer Fridtjof Nansen let his ship freeze into the pack ice on purpose from 1893?
a: To drift with the ice across the Arctic Ocean
To repair the ship in peace
84294.e: Nansen let his ship Fram freeze into the ice and drift with it. That is how he explored the Arctic Ocean.
84294.m: Nansen drifted through the Arctic ice in the Fram.

84295.q: Is there more or less sea ice in the Arctic today than 50 years ago?
84295.e: Satellite images show that the sea ice in summer has become much smaller. This is linked to global warming.
84295.m: The Arctic sea ice keeps shrinking.

84296.q: What happened in Antarctica in 1915 to the ship Endurance of the polar explorer Ernest Shackleton?
a: It was crushed by the pack ice
It was the first ship to reach the South Pole
84296.e: The Endurance got stuck in the ice in Antarctica and was crushed. Even so, all the men of the crew survived.
84296.m: Shackleton's Endurance was crushed by the ice.

84297.q: What happens to the sea level when a lot of ice on land melts?
84297.e: Meltwater from glaciers flows into the sea. This means there is more water and the sea level rises.
84297.m: When ice on land melts, the sea level rises.

84298.q: Which islands are especially threatened by rising sea levels?
84298.e: Most of the islands of the Maldives are only about one metre above the sea. If the water rises, they could be flooded.
84298.m: Low islands are threatened by the rising sea.

84299.q: How do the Netherlands protect their land from the sea?
84299.e: Dykes are long banks of earth and stone. They keep the sea away from the low-lying land.
84299.m: Dykes protect the land from the sea.

84300.q: What does “metres above sea level” mean for a mountain?
a: How high it is above the level of the sea
How far it is from the sea
How deep the sea next to it is
How long it takes to drive to the sea
84300.e: Heights are measured from the surface of the sea. That way all the mountains in the world can be compared.
84300.m: Heights are measured from sea level.

84301.q: Which city in Italy is often under water when the sea is high?
84301.e: Venice is built on many islands in a lagoon. During high water, called “acqua alta”, squares are flooded.
84301.m: Venice is often flooded at high water.

84302.q: What height is sea level on maps?
84302.e: Sea level is the zero point for all heights. Anything higher has a positive height.

84303.q: What can happen more often on coasts when the sea level is higher?
84303.e: If the sea is higher, it gets into the land more easily during storms. Then floods happen more often.
84303.m: A higher sea brings more floods to the coasts.

84304.q: What are the walls of a greenhouse usually made of?
84304.e: The walls have to let the sunlight in. That is why they are made of glass or clear plastic.

84305.q: Why is it warmer in a greenhouse than outside?
a: Sunlight gets in and the heat stays inside
The plants breathe out warm air
There is a fire hidden in the ground
84305.e: The sunlight warms the soil and the plants. The warm air can hardly escape through the glass.
84305.m: In a greenhouse, the sun's warmth is trapped.

84306.q: Which vegetable is often grown in greenhouses in Switzerland?
84306.e: Tomatoes like it warm. In greenhouses they grow even when it is cool outside.
84306.m: Tomatoes grow well in a greenhouse.

84307.q: What is another word for a greenhouse?
84307.e: Greenhouse and glasshouse mean the same thing. Plants are grown in the warmth inside.
84307.m: A greenhouse is also called a glasshouse.

84308.q: What happens in a car that stands in the sun in summer with the windows closed?
a: It stays as warm as outside
84308.e: Just like in a greenhouse, the sun shines through the windows and the heat stays inside. That is why you must never leave children or animals in the car.
84308.m: A car in the sun gets as hot as a greenhouse inside.

84309.q: Why does a gardener open the greenhouse windows on hot days?
a: So it does not get too hot for the plants
84309.e: In strong sunshine it can get too hot in the greenhouse. Fresh air cools the plants down.
84309.m: Letting air in protects greenhouse plants from heat.

84310.q: When is a greenhouse especially useful?
a: In spring, when it is still cold outside
In high summer in great heat
84310.e: In a greenhouse you can sow seeds early in the year. The young plants are protected from frost.
84310.m: A greenhouse protects young plants from the cold.

84311.q: What in the Earth's atmosphere works in a similar way to the glass of a greenhouse?
84311.e: Some gases in the air hold back heat, a bit like glass. This is called the greenhouse effect.
84311.m: Gases in the air keep the Earth warm like a greenhouse.

84312.q: Which metal is steel mainly made from?
84312.e: Steel is iron with a little carbon. This makes it stronger and tougher.
84312.m: Steel is mainly made of iron.

84313.q: Which metal does our blood need to carry oxygen?
84313.e: The red pigment in blood contains iron. It binds oxygen and carries it all round the body.
84313.m: The red pigment in blood contains iron.

84314.q: Where does the iron that nails are made from come from?
84314.e: Iron is found in certain rocks called iron ore. They are dug out of the ground and the iron is melted out.
84314.m: Iron comes from rocks in the ground.

84315.q: Where is iron ore melted into iron?
84315.e: A blast furnace is a huge furnace that gets very hot. Inside it, the ore turns into liquid iron.
84315.m: In a blast furnace, iron ore becomes iron.

84316.q: What happens to iron if it lies outside in the rain for a long time?
84316.e: Water and air attack the iron. Brown rust forms.

84317.q: Which famous tower in Paris is built of iron?
84317.e: The Eiffel Tower was built in 1889 from many thousands of iron parts. They are held together with rivets.
84317.m: The Eiffel Tower in Paris is made of iron.

84318.q: What happens to an iron nail that you put in water?
84318.e: Iron is much heavier than the same amount of water. That is why an iron nail sinks at once.
84318.m: An iron nail sinks in water.

84319.q: What happens if you stroke an iron nail many times in the same direction with a magnet?
84319.e: Stroking turns the nail itself into a weak magnet. Then it can pick up small paper clips.
84319.m: An iron nail can become a magnet itself.

84320.q: What are heavy, dark frying pans often made of?
84320.e: Cast iron is iron that is poured into a mould while liquid. Such pans are heavy and hold the heat for a long time.
84320.m: Heavy frying pans are often made of cast iron.

84321.q: What colour is freshly polished copper?
84321.e: Copper is one of the few metals with a colour of its own. It shines reddish brown.

84323.q: Which reddish metal are some expensive cooking pots made of?
84323.e: Copper pots shine reddish. Cooks like them because they heat up quickly and evenly.
84323.m: Some cooking pots are made of copper.

84324.q: Why are some pan bases made of copper?
84324.e: Copper passes on the heat from the hob quickly. This makes the whole pan evenly hot.

84325.q: Which metal is the outer skin of the Statue of Liberty in New York made of?
84325.e: The Statue of Liberty has a skin of thin copper sheets. It used to shine reddish brown, but today it is green.
84325.m: The Statue of Liberty is made of copper on the outside.

84326.q: What is the period called when people first made tools from copper?
84326.e: Copper was one of the first metals people used. The Copper Age lies at the end of the New Stone Age.
84326.m: In the Copper Age, people made their first tools from copper.

84327.q: What can you easily do with a thin copper wire?
84327.e: Copper is soft and bends well. That is why you can shape figures from copper wire.

84328.q: What is copper wire very often used for in the home?
84328.e: Electric cables contain copper wires. Copper conducts electricity very well.

84329.q: What does pure, polished silver look like?
84329.e: Silver is a bright, white, shiny metal. It reflects light very well.

84330.q: What happens to silver cutlery that lies in the drawer for a long time?
84330.e: Silver reacts with traces of sulphur in the air. This forms a dark layer; we say it tarnishes.
84330.m: Silver tarnishes and goes dark over time.

84331.q: How does tarnished silver become shiny again?
84331.e: When polishing, you rub away the dark layer. Afterwards the silver shines brightly again.
84331.m: Polishing makes tarnished silver beautiful again.

84332.q: Which place gets a silver medal at the Olympic Games?
84332.e: The silver medal is for second place. The winner gets the gold medal.

84333.q: Which metal is more expensive than silver?
84333.e: Gold is much rarer than silver. That is why it costs a great deal more per gram.
84333.m: Gold is more valuable than silver.

84334.q: Which metal conducts electricity best of all?
84334.e: Silver conducts electricity even better than copper. But because it is expensive, copper is usually used for cables.
84334.m: Silver conducts electricity best of all metals.

84335.q: What is the wedding anniversary after 25 years of marriage called?
84335.e: After 25 years of marriage, people celebrate their silver wedding. After 50 years it is the golden wedding.
84335.m: After 25 years, people celebrate their silver wedding.

84336.q: What is silver especially often used for?
84336.e: Silver shines beautifully and does not rust. That is why rings, necklaces and earrings are often made from it.
84336.m: Jewellery is often made from silver.

84337.q: Which of these metals is especially light?
84337.e: Aluminium weighs only about a third as much as the same amount of iron. That is why it is called a light metal.

84338.q: What are many drinks cans made of?
84338.e: Drinks cans are usually made of thin aluminium. They are light and protect the drink well.
84338.m: Many drinks cans are made of aluminium.

84339.q: Which rock is aluminium obtained from?
84339.e: Bauxite is a reddish rock with a lot of aluminium in it. Using a lot of electricity, aluminium is made from it.

84340.q: What are large parts of many aeroplanes made of?
84340.e: An aeroplane has to be strong but still light. That is why many parts are made of aluminium.
84340.m: Many aeroplane parts are made of aluminium.

84341.q: What do you save when you recycle old aluminium?
84341.e: Making new aluminium takes a great deal of electricity. Melting down old aluminium needs only a small part of that.
84341.m: Recycling aluminium saves a lot of energy.

84342.e: In air, aluminium forms a very thin protective layer. This protects the metal, so it does not rust.

84343.q: What are light bike frames often made of?
84343.e: Aluminium bike frames are strong and light. That way you can easily carry the bike.
84343.m: Light bike frames are often made of aluminium.

84344.e: Aluminium is a shiny, silvery grey metal. It looks a bit like silver but is much cheaper.

84345.q: Which small toy figures used to be cast from a soft, silvery metal?
84345.e: Tin figures are made by pouring liquid tin into moulds. Tin soldiers used to be a popular toy.
84345.m: Tin figures are cast from tin.

84346.q: Which of these metals melts at quite a low heat?
84346.e: Tin melts at only about 232 degrees. Iron and copper need well over 1000 degrees.
84346.m: Tin melts at a low heat.

84347.e: Tin is a shiny, silvery white metal. It looks a bit like silver.

84348.q: What do you use to join electric wires when soldering?
84348.e: Solder melts on the hot soldering iron and flows around the wires. As it cools, it sets and holds them together.
84348.m: When soldering, wires are joined with solder.

84349.q: What were many plates, mugs and jugs made of in the past?
84349.e: Tinware used to be found in many households. Today it is often collected as an ornament.
84349.m: In the past, people often ate from tin plates.

84350.q: Which soft metal makes a faint crackling sound when you bend a bar of it?
84350.e: When bending, the tiny crystals in the tin rub against each other. This makes a faint crackle called the ‘tin cry’.
84350.m: Tin crackles when you bend it.

84351.q: What can happen to objects made of pure tin if they are exposed to great cold for a very long time?
84351.e: In great cold, tin can slowly crumble into a grey powder. This is called tin pest.
84351.m: Tin can crumble in great cold.

84352.e: Pure tin is a soft metal. It is easy to bend and shape.

84353.q: Which place gets the bronze medal in a competition?
84353.e: In many competitions the three best get a medal. The bronze medal is for third place.

84354.q: Which period came before the Bronze Age?
84354.e: At first people made tools from stone. Only later did they learn to make bronze.
84354.m: The Stone Age came before the Bronze Age.

84355.e: New bronze shines golden brown. Over time it often becomes darker or greenish.

84356.q: What are many church bells cast from?
84356.e: Bronze bells sound especially beautiful and ring for a long time. This mixture is also called bell bronze.
84356.m: Many church bells are made of bronze.

84357.q: What are many large outdoor monuments and statues made of?
84357.e: Bronze withstands wind and weather for many hundreds of years. That is why monuments are often cast from it.
84357.m: Many monuments are cast in bronze.

84358.e: Bronze is made by mixing liquid metals together. Such a mixture is called an alloy.
84358.m: Bronze is a mixture of metals.

84359.q: Why was bronze better than pure copper for tools?
84359.e: Pure copper is quite soft. Bronze is much harder, so knives and axes stayed sharp for longer.

84360.q: What do you call pouring liquid bronze into a mould?
84360.e: The bronze is melted and poured into a mould. When it has cooled, it has taken on the shape.

84361.q: What were the villages on Swiss lake shores called where people lived in the Bronze Age?
84361.e: The houses stood on wooden stilts on the lake shore. Remains of them can still be found in many Swiss lakes today.
84361.m: In the Bronze Age, people in Switzerland lived in stilt houses.

84362.e: Rust is a reddish brown layer on iron. You can easily recognise it by its colour.

84363.q: Where does a bike rust faster?
84363.e: Iron rusts when water and air get to it. In the rain this happens much faster than in the dry.

84364.q: Which of these metals can rust?
84364.e: Rust only forms on iron and steel. Other metals change in other ways or hardly at all.

84365.q: How do you protect an iron garden gate from rust?
a: You stand it in the sun
84365.e: The paint keeps water and air away from the iron. That way the iron cannot rust so quickly.

84366.q: What happens to iron that rusts for years?
a: It becomes brittle and falls apart
84366.e: Rust eats deeper and deeper into the iron. In the end the iron gets holes and crumbles.

84367.q: Why do cars rust faster in winter?
a: Because of the snow on the roof
84367.e: In winter, salt is spread on Swiss roads. Salty water makes iron rust much faster.
84367.m: Road salt makes cars rust faster.

84368.q: What is the kitchen sink often made of, because it does not rust?
84368.e: Stainless steel is a steel that does not rust. It stays shiny even with lots of water.

84369.q: What helps to stop a bike chain from rusting?
84369.e: The oil forms a film on the chain. That way no water can reach the metal.
84369.m: Oil protects the bike chain from rust.

84370.q: Is rust still the same as iron?
a: No, it is a new substance
No, it is a kind of wood
No, it is a kind of garden soil
84370.e: When iron rusts, it combines with oxygen and water. This makes a completely new substance.

84371.q: On which metal can verdigris form?
84371.e: Verdigris is a green coating on copper. It also forms on metals that contain copper.

84372.q: What forms when copper is in contact with vinegar for a long time?
84372.e: The acid in vinegar attacks the copper. This creates a green coating called verdigris.

84373.q: Why must you never eat or lick verdigris?
84373.e: Verdigris is poisonous. That is why you should not keep food in copper pots with a green coating.

84374.q: What is the correct name for the green layer on old copper roofs?
84374.e: People often call it verdigris, but the correct name for this layer is patina. It forms slowly through air and rain.
84374.m: The green layer on copper roofs is called patina.

84375.q: Why is the green layer on a copper roof not removed?
84375.e: The green layer covers the copper like a coat. Underneath, the metal stays in good condition for many years.
84375.m: The green layer protects the copper roof.

84376.q: What did painters use verdigris for in the past?
84376.e: In the past, painters mixed a bright green paint from verdigris. Today there are non-poisonous paints for this.
84376.m: Verdigris used to be a paint.

84378.e: Brass contains copper. That is why a green coating can form on it too.
84378.m: Verdigris can also form on brass.

84379.q: What is kitchen foil used for?
84379.e: Kitchen foil can be wrapped tightly around food. That keeps it fresh or warm.
84379.m: You wrap food in kitchen foil.

84380.q: Can kitchen foil go in the microwave?
a: Yes, if it is completely smooth
Yes, if the food is cold
84380.e: Metal in the microwave can make sparks. That can damage the appliance or start a fire.
84380.m: Kitchen foil does not belong in the microwave.

84381.q: Which side of kitchen foil can you use?
84381.e: One side is dull only because of the way it is made. Both sides work almost equally well.
84381.m: You can use both sides of kitchen foil.

a: Thinner than a sheet of paper
84382.e: Kitchen foil is only about one hundredth of a millimetre thick. A sheet of paper is much thicker.
84382.m: Kitchen foil is thinner than paper.

84383.q: Why should you not wrap acidic food in kitchen foil?
84383.e: Acid from lemons or tomatoes attacks the foil. This can let aluminium get into the food.
84383.m: You do not wrap acidic food in kitchen foil.

84384.q: In which country did the first aluminium foil factory open in 1910?
84384.e: The first rolling mill for aluminium foil opened in 1910 in Kreuzlingen in the canton of Thurgau. From 1911 the foil also wrapped chocolate.
84384.m: The first aluminium foil was made in Switzerland.

84385.q: What do you do with clean, used kitchen foil in Switzerland?
a: Take it to the aluminium collection
Put it in the waste paper
Throw it in the bottle bank
84385.e: Aluminium can be melted down again and again. That is why clean foil is collected together with aluminium cans.
84385.m: Clean kitchen foil goes to the aluminium collection.

84386.q: What can you easily do with kitchen foil without any tools?
84386.e: Kitchen foil is very thin and soft. You can fold and shape it with your hands.
84386.m: Kitchen foil is easy to shape.

84387.q: What is a tin can for?
a: Keeping food for a long time
84387.e: In the sealed can, food stays good for a long time. No air and no germs can get in.
84387.m: A tin can keeps food for a long time.

84388.q: What do you use to open a tin without a ring pull?
84388.e: A tin opener cuts all the way round the lid. Then you can lift it off.
84388.m: You open tins with a tin opener.

84389.q: What is a tin can usually made of?
84389.e: Most tin cans are made of thin sheet steel. It is strong and protects the food well.
84389.m: Tin cans are usually made of sheet steel.

84390.q: Why does a tin can not rust so quickly?
a: It has a thin layer of tin
It is made of pure iron
84390.e: The sheet steel is covered with a fine layer of tin. This metal is called tinplate.
84390.m: A layer of tin protects tin cans from rust.

84391.q: What can you use to separate steel cans from aluminium cans?
84391.e: A magnet attracts steel but not aluminium. This makes the cans easy to sort.
84391.m: A magnet separates steel cans from aluminium cans.

84392.q: What does it mean if the lid of a tin bulges outwards?
a: The contents may have gone off
84392.e: When germs grow in the tin, they make gas. Then the lid bulges and you must not eat the contents.
84392.m: You throw away a bulging tin.

84393.q: What should you do with an empty tin before taking it to the collection point?
84393.e: Rinsed tins do not smell and do not attract animals. That way they can be recycled easily.
84393.m: You rinse empty tins before recycling them.

84394.q: Why is the food heated inside the sealed tin?
a: So that the tin gets lighter
84394.e: The heat kills the germs in the food. That is why the contents do not go off for so long.
84394.m: Heat kills the germs in the tin.

84395.q: How long does food usually stay good in a sealed tin?
84395.e: Tinned food often keeps for several years. The tin says until when the contents are at least good.
84395.m: Tinned food often keeps for several years.

84396.e: A smith heats metal in the fire until it glows. Then he shapes it with a hammer.

84397.q: What is a smith's workshop called?
84397.e: In the forge there is a fire, an anvil and lots of hammers. That is where the smith works.
84397.m: The smith works in the forge.

84398.q: On which heavy iron block does the smith hammer the metal?
84398.e: The anvil is a heavy block of steel. The smith lays the hot metal on it and hammers it into shape.
84398.m: The smith hammers the metal on the anvil.

84399.q: What does the smith use to hold the red-hot iron?
84399.e: The iron is far too hot to touch. With long tongs the smith holds it safely.
84399.m: The smith holds the hot iron with tongs.

84400.q: Why does the smith make the iron red-hot?
a: So it becomes soft and easy to shape
84400.e: Cold iron is hard and can hardly be shaped. Red-hot iron can be bent and stretched with a hammer.
84400.m: Red-hot iron is easy to shape.

84401.q: What is a smith who fits horseshoes on horses called?
84401.e: The farrier shapes horseshoes and fixes them to the horses' hooves. This protects the hooves.

84403.q: What does the smith use to blow air into the fire to make it hotter?
84403.e: The bellows pump air into the fire. More air makes the fire hotter.
84403.m: The smith makes the fire hotter with bellows.

84404.q: What is the smallest coin in Switzerland (as of 2026)?
84404.e: The 1-centime coin was withdrawn in 2007, and the 2-centime coin even earlier. Today the 5-centime coin is the smallest coin.
84404.m: The smallest Swiss coin is the 5-centime coin.

84405.q: What colour is the Swiss 5-centime coin?
84405.e: The 5-centime coin is made of a mixture containing copper and aluminium. That is why it shines golden yellow.

84406.q: Which female figure can be seen on Swiss 1-franc coins?
84406.e: Helvetia is a female figure who stands for Switzerland. She is shown standing with a spear and shield.

84407.q: In which city are Swiss coins made?
84407.e: The Swiss mint is called Swissmint. It is in Bern.
84407.m: Swiss coins are made in Bern.

84408.e: A machine presses the picture into a small metal disc with great force. This is called minting.

84409.q: What is the 5-franc coin often called in Switzerland?
84409.e: The 5-franc coin is the largest Swiss coin. In everyday life it is called the Fünfliber.
84409.m: The 5-franc coin is also called the Fünfliber.

84410.q: What are the two sides called when you toss a coin?
84410.e: One side shows the value, the number. The other side often shows a head or a picture.
84410.m: When you toss a coin, it is heads or tails.

84411.q: Which metals is the Swiss 1-franc coin made of?
84411.e: The shiny silver franc coins are made of copper and nickel. Until 1967 they were made of silver.
84411.m: The 1-franc coin is made of copper and nickel.

84609.q: What do you take a digital photo with?
84609.e: A digital camera takes in light and saves the picture as a file. Mobile phones and tablets have a camera like this built in too.
84609.m: You take digital photos with a camera, including a phone camera.

84610.q: Unlike an old camera, what does a digital camera no longer need?
84610.e: Old cameras recorded the picture on film. A digital camera, on the other hand, saves the photo as a file.
84610.m: A digital camera saves photos as a file without film.

84611.q: What is the button on a camera that you press to take a photo called?
84611.e: When you press the shutter button, the camera takes the picture. On a phone the shutter button is often a round button on the screen.
84611.m: You take a photo with the shutter button.

84612.q: Through which part of the camera does the light come in?
84612.e: The lens is made of glass lenses. It directs the light into the inside of the camera.
84612.m: Light gets into the camera through the lens.

84613.q: What is the flash on a camera for?
a: It makes the photo more colourful
84613.e: When it is too dark, the flash lights up very briefly. That makes the photo brighter.
84613.m: The flash helps when it is too dark to take photos.

84614.q: You photograph a person with the sun shining brightly behind them. What does the person often look like in the photo?
84614.e: Bright light from behind is called backlight. The camera adjusts to the bright sun, so the person turns out dark.
84614.m: With backlight, the person in the photo is often too dark.

84615.q: What should you do before you send on a photo of another person?
84615.e: Everyone may decide for themselves where photos of them are shown. That is why you always ask first.
84615.m: I only show photos of others if they agree.

84616.q: What often happens if the camera wobbles while you take a photo?
84616.e: If the camera moves while taking the picture, the picture smudges. That is why you hold the camera still.
84616.m: If you hold the camera still, you get sharper photos.

84617.q: What do you do when you crop a photo?
84617.e: When cropping, you remove parts at the edge of the picture. That moves the important part to the centre.
84617.m: When cropping, you remove unimportant edges of a photo.

84618.q: A photo is much too dark. What do you turn up in the photo editor?
84618.e: With the brightness slider the whole picture gets brighter. Then you can see more again.
84618.m: You make photos that are too dark brighter with the brightness slider.

84619.q: A photo is upside down. What do you do in the photo editor?
84619.e: With the rotate function you can turn the picture a quarter turn or a half turn. Then it is the right way up.
84619.m: You can rotate crooked or upside-down photos in a photo editor.

84620.q: In a flash photo the eyes glow red. Which function helps?
84620.e: The flash reflects in the eye and makes it red. Red-eye correction turns those spots dark again.
84620.m: You can remove red eyes in flash photos with a special function.

84621.q: Which command undoes your last editing step?
84621.e: The Undo command takes back the last step. It often has an arrow symbol pointing to the left.
84621.m: With “Undo” you can take back a mistake straight away.

84622.q: Why is it best to save an edited photo as a copy?
84622.e: If you save as a copy, the unchanged photo is kept as well. That way you can start again later.
84622.m: If you save as a copy, you keep the original.

84623.q: What happens when you flip a photo in the photo editor?
84623.e: When you flip it, the picture looks as it would in a mirror. What was on the left before is on the right afterwards.
84623.m: When you flip a picture, its sides are swapped.

84624.q: What can you add to a photo in a photo editing app?
84624.e: Many apps let you put writing, stickers or frames on a photo. That way you can design an invitation, for example.
84624.m: In a photo editing app you can put text and stickers on photos.

84625.q: Which tool in a drawing program paints free lines like a real brush?
84625.e: With the brush you draw coloured lines wherever you move the mouse. You can set how thick it is.
84625.m: With the brush you paint free lines.

84626.q: Which tool fills a whole area with colour in one go?
84626.e: If you click with the paint bucket inside a closed area, the whole area is filled. If the area is not closed, the colour leaks out.
84626.m: With the paint bucket you fill areas in one click.

84627.q: Which tool do you use to remove something you have painted in a drawing program?
84627.e: The eraser deletes lines wherever you move over them. The background colour shows there again.
84627.m: The eraser removes painting in a drawing program.

84628.q: What do you usually draw with in a drawing program on a computer?
84628.e: With the mouse you move the pointer over the picture. If you hold the button down, it paints.
84628.m: On a computer you often draw with the mouse.

84629.q: What can you use to draw especially precisely on a tablet?
84629.e: A stylus has a tip that the screen recognises. With it you paint more precisely than with your finger.
84629.m: With a stylus you draw very precisely on a tablet.

84630.q: Where do you choose the colour in a drawing program?
84630.e: The colour palette shows lots of colour squares. Clicking one chooses the colour for the brush.
84630.m: In the colour palette you choose your painting colour.

84631.q: Which tool do you use to draw completely straight lines?
84631.e: With the line tool you set the start and end, and the program joins them in a straight line. Freehand this rarely works so precisely.
84631.m: For straight lines you use the line tool.

84632.q: What is the simple drawing program that has come with Windows for a long time called?
84632.e: Paint has been part of Windows since 1985. You can draw and edit simple pictures with it.
84632.m: Paint is a simple drawing program from Windows.

84633.q: What are pictures in pixel art made of?
84633.e: In pixel art you build the picture out of lots of small, clearly visible squares. Each square is a pixel.
84633.m: Pixel art builds pictures out of small squares.

84634.e: Pixel is a made-up word from “picture element”. It is a single dot of a picture.
84634.m: A pixel is a single dot of a picture.

84635.q: A pixel art picture is 8 pixels wide and 8 pixels high. How many pixels does it have?
84635.e: There are 8 rows with 8 pixels each. 8 times 8 makes 64.
84635.m: The number of pixels is width times height.

84636.q: Where do you see pixel art especially often?
84636.e: Early computers could only show a few dots. That is why characters in old video games looked blocky.
84636.m: Old video games are famous for their pixel art.

84637.q: What can you use to make pixel art without a computer?
84637.e: Ironing beads are placed on a pegboard in rows. That makes a picture out of lots of dots of the same size.
84637.m: Ironing beads or squared paper are good for pixel art too.

84638.q: How many colours does a single pixel have?
84638.e: A pixel is the smallest part of a picture. It always has just one single colour.
84638.m: Each pixel has exactly one colour.

84639.q: What happens when a picture is made of more pixels?
a: It becomes finer and more precise
84639.e: With more dots you can show finer shapes. With few pixels a picture looks blocky.
84639.m: The more pixels a picture has, the finer it can be.

84640.q: On which paper is it especially easy to draw pixel art by hand?
84640.e: Squared paper is divided into small squares. You can colour in each square with one colour, like a pixel.
84640.m: On squared paper each square becomes a pixel.

a: A picture of what the screen is showing
A photo of the computer cable
A photo that you print out
84641.e: A screenshot records exactly what can be seen on the screen at that moment. You do not need a camera for it.
84641.m: A screenshot saves a picture of the screen.

84642.q: Which word is made of “screen” and “shot” and means a picture of the screen?
84642.e: A shot is a picture you take. Screen plus shot makes screenshot.
84642.m: A picture of the screen is called a screenshot.

84643.q: Which key takes a screenshot on many Windows computers?
84643.e: The Print Screen key copies a picture of the screen.
84643.m: With the Print Screen key you take a screenshot on a Windows computer.

84644.q: Where do you usually find a screenshot on a phone?
84644.e: The phone saves screenshots like other pictures. That is why they appear with the photos.
84644.m: On a phone, screenshots end up with the photos.

84645.q: What can a screenshot be useful for?
84645.e: With a screenshot you can show someone exactly what is happening on the device. That way another person can help better.
84645.m: With a screenshot you can show what you see on the screen.

84646.q: May you simply send a screenshot of a private chat to others?
84646.e: A chat is a private conversation. Forwarding it without permission can hurt others.
84646.m: I only pass on other people's private messages with permission.

84647.q: What kind of file is a screenshot?
84647.e: A screenshot is a still picture. That is why it is saved as an image file.
84647.m: A screenshot is saved as a picture.

84648.q: What is it called when you record the screen like a film?
84648.e: With a screen recording, everything that happens on the screen is saved as a video. A screenshot, on the other hand, only shows one moment.
84648.m: A screen recording saves the screen as a video.

84649.e: A video shows pictures that move. Usually you hear sound with it too.
84649.m: A video shows moving pictures, often with sound.

84650.q: What is a video actually made of?
84650.e: A video shows lots of pictures one after another very quickly. Our eyes see a smooth movement.
84650.m: A video is made of lots of single pictures shown quickly.

84651.q: Which symbol does the button for playing a video usually have?
84651.e: The triangle pointing to the right means play.

84652.q: What do two vertical lines on a video button mean?
84652.e: With the pause button the video stops. If you press it again, it carries on from the same place.

84653.q: What does a square on a video button usually mean?
84653.e: The square ends playback. After that the video often starts again from the beginning.
84653.m: A square on a button means stop.

84654.q: What is it called when you cut out parts of a video and put them together again?
84654.e: In video editing you remove boring bits and arrange the scenes. There are special programs and apps for this.
84654.m: In video editing a video is shortened and put together.

84655.q: How do you hold your phone so that a video is wide like on a television?
84655.e: A television is wider than it is tall. If you hold your phone sideways, the video has the same wide shape.
84655.m: For a wide video you hold your phone sideways.

84656.q: Roughly how many pictures per second does a video show?
84656.e: Many videos show 25 or 30 pictures every second. That is so fast that the movement looks smooth.
84656.m: A video shows about 25 to 30 pictures every second.

84657.q: What is the text at the bottom of a video that shows what is being said called?
84657.e: Subtitles write what is said as text on the screen. They help, for example, people who cannot hear well.
84657.m: Subtitles show what is said as text.

84658.q: What do you record sounds and voices with?
84658.e: A microphone turns sound into electrical signals. The device can then save them.
84658.m: You record sounds with a microphone.

84659.q: What do you use to play back a sound recording out loud in the room?
84659.e: A loudspeaker turns saved sounds back into sound you can hear. With headphones you listen on your own.

a: A programme to listen to on the internet
A photo album on the internet
84660.e: You can listen to a podcast on the internet whenever you like. There are often lots of episodes on one topic.
84660.m: A podcast is a listening programme from the internet.

84661.q: What can disturb a sound recording outdoors especially badly?
84661.e: Wind blows into the microphone and makes loud rushing noises. A windshield made of foam or fur helps against this.
84661.m: Wind can make a sound recording outdoors rush loudly.

84662.q: Where does a voice recording work best?
84662.e: In a quiet room there are no disturbing noises. That way the voice sounds clear.
84662.m: For good sound recordings you look for a quiet place.

84663.q: What does the jagged line that appears on the screen while recording show?
84663.e: The jagged line shows the sound wave. Big peaks mean loud sounds, small peaks quiet sounds.
84663.m: Big peaks in the sound wave mean loud sounds.

84664.q: What is a short sound recording that you send in a chat called?
84664.e: With a voice message you speak into the phone instead of writing. The other person listens to it later.
84664.m: A voice message is a spoken message in a chat.

84665.q: Which is a well-known format for sound files?
